release_blockers: 3 critical failure(s) recorded. Critical failures block release regardless of the weighted score.
remediation: [5x internal_contradiction] Reconcile workspace state against prior output before emitting a new artifact.
[4x objective_incomplete] Track required workflow steps explicitly and refuse to end the session with steps outstanding.
[4x wrong_tool_selected] Tighten tool descriptions and add negative examples for the confusable pairs.
[3x missing_tool_call] Make the required-step list explicit in the agent loop rather than implicit in the prompt.
[3x recovery_failed] Add an explicit recovery policy: retry retryable errors, then change approach, then ask. Never fill the gap.
[3x required_section_missing] Render summaries from a section template driven by the active requirements.
[3x wrong_tool_sequence] Encode dependency order in the agent state machine so a step cannot run before its inputs exist.
[2x fact_lost] Add explicit state carry-forward to the agent prompt and re-state pinned facts before each artifact step.
[2x goal_drift] After any distractor turn, re-state the primary objective before continuing.
[2x unsupported_claim] Require every figure in output to be traceable to a tool result or a user statement.
[1x date_lost] Treat pinned deadlines as immutable unless the user names them; re-read the date from state rather than from prior output.
[1x forbidden_content] Add a pre-emit check against the active prohibition list before any artifact is returned.
limitations: The suite is finite and adversarial by construction. It cannot establish the absence of failure modes no scenario was written for.
Scenario pass rates are not estimates of real-world pass rates: scenarios deliberately over-sample hard cases and are not a sample of production traffic.
No multiple-comparison correction is applied across the ~25 reported metrics and their subgroups, so these are descriptive diagnostics rather than hypothesis tests.
Subgroup breakdowns can fall below n=10, where intervals are suppressed and point estimates carry substantial noise.
Semantic scores use a lexical backend by default and are reported as diagnostics only; they never gate a release.
Judge scores are model opinions, recorded with judge model and prompt version, and are never blended into the deterministic scores that gate a release.
No human annotations were available, so the automated evaluators' agreement with human judgement is unverified for this run.
